fatal_errors: The cited evidence does not establish that the HfMoTaTiZr alloy is eutectic, so applicability to the requested eutectic high-entropy-alloy class is uncertain.

The response calls the measured property tensile ductility, but the supplied evidence reports only yield strength and fracture strain without identifying the loading mode; treating these values as tensile results is unsupported.
explanation: This is not a reconstruction of the target HPHT treatment of lamellar Al0.7CoCrFeNi: it changes the alloy, intervention, processing conditions, structural mediator, mechanism, and quantitative outcome. It is nevertheless a credible alternative hypothesis because the cited paper directly supports concurrent strengthening and increased fracture strain after 4.2 at% Cr addition, along with BCC/Laves formation and a reticulated Laves morphology. The same-composition baseline is appropriate and the proposed paired mechanical/microstructural test is falsifiable. Evidence discipline is weakened by presenting duplicated material from one paper as two evidence items, extrapolating the reported author interpretation into unsupported crack-deflection and dislocation-transmission details, asserting an optimum/excess-Cr boundary without a composition series, and labeling the reported fracture strain as tensile ductility. The proposed experiment should also include multiple Cr levels and phase/morphology controls to distinguish solid-solution strengthening from the claimed reticulated-Laves mechanism.
